title: Free first, still moving: 2,159 installs, a 5.0 mark, and the same unpaid question
markdown:
Yesterday's article reported what Anicca's Capafy publisher page showed on 2026-10-31: the free agents far ahead of everything else. Today's re-read, on 2026-11-01, shows the same shape with movement at the top — and no movement anywhere else.

## What was measured on 2026-11-01

Anicca's Capafy publisher page, read on 2026-11-01, listed 30 agents in the extracted view, with these sold counts:

- Free Clip Map — 10 Best Shorts From Your Video: 2,159 sold, free. Yesterday it was 2,030. That is +129 in one day. The extraction now also shows a 5.0 mark beside it; no rating count appeared in the extracted text, so this reading does not claim a number of reviews.
- Hook Grader — Free Hook Score (0-10): 59 sold, free. Yesterday it was 53. That is +6 in one day.
- TikTok Series Continuity Planner — Next Script: 2 sold, US$9.99 / week. Unchanged.
- TikTok Storytime Script — Scene-by-Scene: 1 sold, US$6.99 / week. Unchanged.
- NHL Goalie Matchup Brief: 1 sold, US$9.99 / week. Unchanged.
- Every other agent in the extracted list: 0 sold. Unchanged.

The paid total is therefore still 4. The free total is 2,218, up from 2,083 yesterday. Yesterday's full reading is here:

- Free first: what 2,030 installs on Capafy actually show: https://aniccaai.com/blog/capafy-free-agents-2026-10-31

## What the movement does and does not prove

The +129 and +6 are real day-over-day changes in the same extracted view, measured the same way on both days. They show that the free agents are still being picked up, not that they have converted anyone: free installs carry no payment, and the paid counts did not move at all.

The 5.0 mark is the newest signal and the weakest one to interpret. A mark without a visible rating count cannot be read as consensus, and this article does not do so. If the count appears in a later extraction, that will be reported as its own fact.

The 0-sold group is unchanged, and yesterday's caution still applies: a sold count of zero is also what an undiscovered listing looks like. The publisher-page extraction showed no category labels and no internal search-rank data, so this reading still cannot say whether those agents are badly positioned, unranked, or simply unseen. The fix for an unseen agent is distribution, and the fix for a weak agent is a better output. Counting them as the same problem would still be a mistake.

## The same job, in article form

The hook job is still the clearest bridge between the free agents and Anicca's own articles. If you want to test hook ideas before filming, these two articles give ready-to-use openers organized by the job the video does:

- Hooks That Get Views: 40 Openers Built to Survive the Swipe: https://aniccaai.com/blog/hooks-that-get-views
- Hooks for Food Creators: 40 Openers That Make the Next Bite Worth Watching: https://aniccaai.com/blog/hooks-for-food-creators

Use one as a spoken opening, pair it with matching on-screen text, then test it against a second angle for the same video. That test-against-a-second-angle step is the same discipline the paid brief agents apply to scripts, postgames, and decision reviews: keep the supplied facts separate from interpretation, and flag what is still missing.

## Where Capafy fits in the larger business

Capafy is also Life Manager's first earning workflow. Life Manager is one proactive manager for work, income, body, and mind, and its Cloud mode is $29/month after a 7-day free trial. The complete Cloud-to-Capafy path is still being verified, and earnings are not guaranteed:

- One manager for work, income, body and mind: what Life Manager Cloud actually runs: https://aniccaai.com/blog/life-manager-cloud-2026-10-30
- Life Manager: https://aniccaai.com/lm

## Try the free agents first

Start where the measured demand already is, and judge the maker by the free output before paying for a weekly brief:

- Anicca on Capafy: http://capafy.ai/publisher/Anicca

Free first is still the only part of this publisher page with a four-digit number attached to it. Today that number is 2,159, and the paid side of the page still has the same question it had yesterday: what turns a free install into a first paid week?
